none_means: No qualifying prior reference verified; not a proof of novelty.

results.references: - Peter Richtárik and Xun Qian. [Broximal Gradient Descent in General Norms: Convergence without Fejér Monotonicity](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24645v1). 2026 (arXiv v1). Complexity: warm-started radius halving reaches objective gap $\varepsilon$ in $O(K)$ exact gradient calls and $O(K+\log_4^+(r^2(8L^2/\mu+6L)/\varepsilon))$ local linear minimization calls, including rejected trials. For initial gap $\Delta_0=f(x_0)-\inf_C f>\varepsilon>0$, $K=\lfloor\log_4(1+6\Delta_0/(Lr^2))\rfloor+\lceil\log(\Delta_0/\varepsilon)/\log(1+\mu/(25L))\rceil$, and $\log_4^+(t)=\max\{0,\log_4 t\}$. If $\Delta_0\le\varepsilon$, the initial point already meets the target.

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: The objective may be nonconvex. It is bounded below on a nonempty closed convex feasible set C, differentiable at every point of C, and satisfies ‖Df(y)−Df(x)‖_* ≤ L‖y−x‖ for x,y ∈ C.

problem_class.label: pl
problem_class.details: For every x ∈ C, 2μ(f(x)−inf_C f) ≤ (inf_{n ∈ N_C(x)} ‖Df(x)+n‖_*)², where N_C(x) consists of the dual functionals n satisfying n(z−x) ≤ 0 for all z ∈ C.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: At any feasible query x, oracle 0 returns the exact Fréchet derivative Df(x) as a continuous linear functional for every history and seed.

oracle.label: linear_minimization
oracle.details: Given x ∈ C, any radius ρ ≥ 0, and any dual functional g, oracle 1 returns an exact minimizer of g over C ∩ {z : ‖z−x‖ ≤ ρ}. Ties may be resolved using the history and seed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: non_euclidean_geometry
distinctive_assumptions.details: The norm on E is arbitrary. It defines the local oracle balls, and its dual norm measures both gradient variation and the normal-cone residual.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real normed space of arbitrary dimension.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The algorithm receives E, L > 0, r > 0, and the feasible starting point x₀. The PL modulus μ > 0, initial gap bound Δ ≥ f(x₀)−inf_C f, and target ε > 0 enter the oracle budgets but are hidden from the algorithm.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/BroxGeneralNormConstrainedPL.lean, Public, Params, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, and spec.admissible. LongTails/Template.lean, Convergence.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The returned point x must satisfy f(x)−inf_C f ≤ ε.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The same returned point must belong to C.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: Feasibility and the objective-gap bound must hold jointly with probability one under the product of the algorithm and oracle seed laws at the prescribed per-oracle budgets.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup combines a constrained PL inequality on the dual normal-cone residual with exact linear minimization over variable-radius feasible balls in an arbitrary norm. Gradient calls and local minimization calls have separate budgets, and the algorithm receives neither the PL modulus nor the initial gap bound.
